title: docs(guides): add a guide explaining how to use react-router with ris
body:
Contains the react-router example within a guide and re-document props on InstantSearch.

history stays undocumented, and the idea is to never expose it (and remove it from the props in the end)

comments.body: By analyzing the blame information on this pull request, we identified @Morhaus, @bobylito and @vvo to be potential reviewers

What about we remove the `urlSync` option right away (we are in beta, that's the right time)? In the react-world there is a high probability people will want to use a custom routing solution rather than ours.

The example you created provides a nicer interface and allow more customization easily (like doing `/search/some+products?filters=..` or renaming any parameter).
Yes we can remove the urlSync props and readd it later if needed. I'll remove the threshold one as well.

So we're fine with the api contrary to what I said earlier. I updated the example accordingly. Feel free to try it/make your suggestion if you think of an easier way. 

On another PR, what I want to do, is changing our props validation. Basically if a user provides a state we should make sure the onStateChange is their, the createURL remaining optional. But a user must be able to provide an onStateChange function without an associated state. Do we agree on this ?

> But a user must be able to provide an onStateChange function without an associated state. Do we agree on this ?

Yes!
I like this a lot! We are going the right way in doing this and externalizing state synchronization in the url.
